title: Supreme Gratitude: Join Us for a Thank-You Letter Party!
description:
Let’s show Justices Allison Riggs and Anita Earls how much we appreciate them!

As we watched Justice Riggs finally being sworn in, all we could think was that her reward for fighting so hard to make sure every vote was counted is that she now has to work with the very people who tried to steal the election from her.

And we can only imagine how distressing it is for Justice Earls, a Black woman, to go to work every day with colleagues who filed ethics complaints against her for merely acknowledging the existence of racial bias in our judicial system. Talk about a toxic work environment!

But we know that a little support goes a long way, and these badass justices deserve all the love and light we can send their way. So let’s show them we’ve got their backs by writing letters of support – and maybe a dash of humor – to brighten their days and thank them for fighting the good fight!

Join us at Ponysaurus on Thursday, June 12 at 6PM for a postcard/letter-writing party! We’ll provide pizza and have some postcards, stationery, and art supplies on hand (or feel free to bring your own). After the party, we’ll collect the letters and mail them to the Court where Justices Earls and Riggs show up every day to fight for our rights!

title: Access Denied: The Growing Threat to Press Freedom in the U.S.
description: Join Sherman Smith, Editor-in-Chief of the Kansas Reflector (a States Newsroom affiliate), for a vital conversation on the growing restrictions facing journalists at both the state and federal levels. From blocked access to legislative chambers in states like Kansas, Texas, and New York, to increasing hurdles at the White House, Sherman will explore how these trends threaten press freedom and public accountability. Drawing on recent developments—including legal battles over content regulation, the role of the White House Correspondents’ Association, and media shakeups like the CBS News Director’s resignation—this webinar confronts a chilling question: What happens to democracy when reporters are silenced? Don’t miss this urgent discussion, hosted by one of the nation’s leading voices in independent journalism.

Contact Jane Comer or Mary Mann or Debra Ucci at 254-301-7648 to volunteer to register voters.

8:45am - Truck arrives, signs in and moves to our spot in the line up.

9:00am - Volunteers arrive, decorate the truck and get ready to roll.

We are excited to join the Juneteenth festival for the second time with a Citizen Action booth!

Volunteers are needed at the Citizen Action booth to share with community members about our economic and racial justice campaigns including the 13th Forward campaign to End Slavery in New York, Housing Justice for All, and Healthcare for All.

What is Juneteenth? Juneteenth is a National Holiday that marks the day in 1865 when a group of enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, finally learned that they were free from the institution of slavery. This was almost two-and-a-half years after President Abraham Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation. As much as Juneteenth represents freedom, it also represents how emancipation and justice was delayed for enslaved people.

title: State of the State Rally
description:
Join us as we raise our voices and signs together to show support for public education and our democratic rights, both of which are currently under attack in the state legislature.

Public Education: The proposed Ohio state budget would cost Westerville schools $110 million in revenue over the next year, penalize our district for fiscal responsibility, take billions from public schools and give to private schools, result in substantial cuts to many student services and programs, and force our district to ask voters for property tax increases every year.

Democratic Rights: The Ohio "SAVE Act" would severely restrict citizens' rights to vote and participate in democracy, such as by eliminating voter-registration drives and online registration, making voting more difficult for those who have changed their names for reasons such as marriage or adoption, increasing the difficulty for citizens to amend the state Constitution or propose laws through the petition process, and threatening volunteer petition circulators with the potential for politically-motivated investigations.

Organizers will have handouts addressing both issues, with contact information for elected officials so you can tell them to stop playing games with our students' futures and our democratic rights.
We will gather in front of Westerville City Hall and spread out along South State Street. Our recent rallies have been peaceful and enthusiastic, resulting in positive experiences for participants, people driving by, and local merchants.

Please help us keep our event safe by observing the following best practices:
- Sidewalks: Stay on sidewalks while being considerate and leaving a path for others to pass through. Should an area become overcrowded, a marshal may ask participants to further spread out.
- Street Crossing: Refrain from crossing State Street repeatedly, especially at the crosswalk in front of City Hall.
- Business Access: Be sure to keep clear of local business entrances.
- Counter-Protestors: Do not engage. Stay safe. Walk away, and notify a marshal if need be.

Marshals will be stationed throughout to help keep people safe, keep paths clear, and lead chants.

** Additionally, please consider supporting our many local businesses on State Street and along the side streets- do a little shopping, grab a coffee, or have lunch before or after the rally.

Guest speaker: Justice Anita Earls of the NC Supreme Court. The rally starts at noon and will be followed by an orderly march to The Leaf at Durham Central Park for refreshments and a gathering of community groups to guide, educate and inform you on actions YOU can take.

12:00 Noon Location: Bull Plaza, also known as CCB Plaza (201 Corcoran Street): Rally with special guest speaker Justice Anita Earls who is running in 2026 for reelection to the North Carolina Supreme Court.

The rally portion will last about one hour. We then will organize the crowd for a Group March on sidewalks to The Leaf, the grassy area of Durham Central Park. Marshals with march route will guide folks.

Gathering at The Leaf in Durham Central Park (between Foster Street and Rigsbee Avenue). We enter at the skate park side at 505 Rigsbee Avenue for refreshments, songs, education and activist opportunities. Please come meet the groups who are working to protect our community
and our democracy. This gathering will end at 3:30 at the latest.

Co-sponsored by Durham Democrats and Engaged Durhamites for Democracy.

Dress for the weather. We will be outdoors on a June day in Durham with little or no shade.

With the event running from noon until 3:30 remember to eat and to hydrate before coming to
the rally at noon.

SIGNS Stay tuned for links to downable graphics and messages for signs. If you make your own, please remember that media cannot photograph off color language.

PARKING:
***Chapel Hill Street Parking Garage 326 E Chapel Hill St, Durham, NC 27701
***Corcoran Street Parking Garage 110 Corcoran St, Durham, NC 27701
***Durham Centre Parking Garage 300 W Morgan St, Durham, NC 27701

BATHROOMS:
***No port-a-potties available. Bathroom access is limited.
***Durham Central Park under the pavillion 501 Foster St, Durham, NC 27701 (6 min walk)
***Durham County Main Library has bathrooms 300 N Roxboro St, Durham, NC 27701 (8 min
walk)

HANDICAP ACCESS:
***Handicap parking extremely limited. Consider being dropped off early.
***No stairs. Just regular sidewalks with normal curb ramps.
***Expect large crowds. No seating. Get there early to find a place on the plaza to be and bring
your own chair if necessary.

title: NO KINGS Vallejo Benicia Indivisible
description:
**In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings.**
NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.


🚨**On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets nationwide. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.**🚨


The flag doesn’t belong to Donald Trump. It belongs to us. We’re not watching history happen. We’re making it.


**On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.**
Check out nokings.org for more information.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Democratic Women of Comal County (DWCC) June Meeting
description: This is the monthly meeting of the Democratic Women of Comal County (DWCC). Our organization helps educate and bring awareness to local, state, and national issues impacting Comal County Democrats as well as encouraging and providing support for humanitarian efforts in our community. Our June meeting includes a PANEL DISCUSSION with Sally Duval, Maggie Ellis, Dr. Merrie Fox, and Julie Sanders, moderated by Ashlea Allsup.

title: Newburgh Canvass for Endorsed Candidates
description:
Join us on Saturday, May 31, at 11:30am for our canvass to elect our endorsed candidates in the June 24 primary election! We'll be doorknocking in support of (from right to left) Gabrielle Hill for Orange County Legislature, District 6; Giselle Martinez, Newburgh City Council Ward 1; and Ramona Monteverde, Newburgh City Council, Ward 2; Tamika Stewart, Newburgh City Council, Ward 3; Ronald Zorrilla, Newburgh City Council, Ward 4; and Genesis Ramos, Orange County Legislature, District 4.

Please download the Minivan app and be ready to doorknock!
